title: Burst fingerprinting reveals heterogeneous kernel score decay; action items for mitigations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a sustained customer traffic wave on 2025-02-17 we observed a repeated pattern of p95/p99 latency step-ups tied to mixed short- and long-sequence requests arriving in tight microbursts. The runtimes kernel scoring mechanism decayed confidence for higher-throughput fused kernels when confronted with interleaved short-sequence traffic; subsequent scheduling favored safer but higher-latency kernels and triggered batch preemption paths. This ticket captures the investigative findings, concrete mitigations landed or proposed, and next steps for monitoring and release gating.

Root-cause hypothesis:
- The schedulers adaptive kernel score decay logic assumes stable sequence-length distribution over short windows. Microbursts with heterogeneous shapes (chat typing + background embeddings) caused the score estimator to underweight fused/optimized kernels.
- A combination of conservative probe backoff and the eviction heuristics caused warmed KV-cache state to be lost, amplifying the latency penalty when the fused path was re-selected.
- Autoscale and admission control thresholds allowed bursts to push workers into a transient state where kernel fallback decisions cascaded across the pool.

Impact observed:
- 2025-02-17 03:12-03:47 UTC: repeatable p99 spikes from baseline 180ms to 750-950ms on affected model family (open-7b variants).
- Approx 22% higher token CPU/GPU utilization during windows due to suboptimal kernels and rewarm overheads.
- Several customer endpoints experienced degraded tail latency; one enterprise customer reported timeouts and escalated to CX.

Non-goal:
- This ticket does not aim to redesign the kernel scoring algorithm from first principles; it focuses on stabilizing score decay, improving microburst detection, and adding safety layers that can be shipped quickly.
observations: Grafana traces show correlation between sudden short-sequence arrival rate increase and immediate kernel-score drop for fused-attn kernels.
KV-cache eviction rate increased by 3x during bursts; rewarm time accounts for 40-60ms of added latency per request in the worst windows.
Canary cluster with increased probe smoothness did not exhibit the cascade, indicating probe hysteresis tuning reduces risk.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use load-generator emulating mixed clients: 70% short (<=64 tokens) rapid bursts, 30% long (>=512 tokens) steady traffic.
2) Configure concurrency to 120% of baseline per-worker admission to force microburst scheduling contention.
3) Observe kernel-score telemetry for fused-attn and fallback kernel switches within the 5-10s burst windows.
4) Capture KV-cache hit/miss and batch admission logs from the affected worker nodes.
action_items: AI-1: Implement burst fingerprinting metric (token-length distribution sketch per 2s window) and expose to Console - owner Marco - ETA 2025-03-04 - status: In Progress
AI-2: Add transient probe hysteresis (soft floor) to prevent immediate score decay for kernels with recent warm KV-cache - owner Priya Rao - ETA 2025-03-10 - status: Planned
AI-3: Short-term admission-control tweak: tighter microburst admission cap to prevent cascade; deploy to canary cluster - owner Daniel Kim - ETA 2025-03-02 - status: Done (canary)
AI-4: Create regression test harness that replays mixed-burst traces in CI with synthetic KV-warmup simulation - owner SRE team (lead: Elena Morales) - ETA 2025-03-18 - status: Planned
AI-5: Post-deploy telemetry dashboard and alert: auto-tune thresholds when burst fingerprint entropy exceeds 0.6 - owner Observability (lead: Johan Li) - ETA 2025-03-08 - status: In Progress
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Initial incident review completed. Captured traces and KV-cache metrics; filing this follow-up to track mitigations that do not require a major runtime refactor.

2025-02-20 - Marco Gutierrez: Reproduced locally with synthetic generator and confirmed probe hysteresis prevents the worst fallbacks. Draft PR started for a minimal hysteresis change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime/pull/4212

2025-02-24 - Elena Morales (SRE): Canary admission-control tweak deployed to canary cluster; observed p99 reduction from ~820ms to ~230ms during synthetic bursts. Link to canary run dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/microburst-canary

2025-02-28 - Priya Rao: Design proposal for KV-aware probe hysteresis posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Microburst+Hysteresis+Design. Requesting design review from Runtime and Observability leads.

2025-03-01 - Johan Li: Working on dashboard panels and alert rules. Added burst fingerprint entropy generator to the emulator and landed initial Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/def456/burst-fingerprint-overview

2025-03-02 - Marco Gutierrez: Merged short-term probe backoff PR to canary: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime/pull/4238. Observability flagged edge cases where blended workloads still produce rare deviations; follow-on AI added.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Increasing probe hysteresis can delay legitimate kernel fallback when a kernel is truly failing; mitigate with telemetry and a capped decay window.
Tighter admission caps reduce throughput headroom for large steady workloads; we will gate rollout behind Canary and customer-impact analysis.
Adding fingerprinting and entropy alerts increases observability costs and potential false positives; thresholds must be tuned with production data.
next_steps: 1) Complete AI-1 (burst fingerprint metric) and wire it to Console heatmaps for cross-team visibility.
2) Run 72h canary with probe hysteresis + admission tweak on two model families (open-7b, opt-6.7b) and report tail metrics.
3) Land regression harness into CI and add nightly mixed-burst replay tests.
4) Plan rollout to production with a staged ramp and post-rollout monitoring playbook.
